name: Character.AI
tagline: Chat and roleplay with user-created AI characters, each with its own persona, voice and backstory.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; the paid tier has historically been around 9.99 per month but the number here is unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanic is a system prompt, a chat history, and a streaming text box, which an agent will hand you in an afternoon. Point it at Ollama locally or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and you have private, uncensored-by-your-own-settings roleplay with characters you wrote yourself, which for a lot of people is the entire point. What you cannot rebuild is the several million character cards other people made, the discovery surface that finds them, and models specifically tuned to stay in persona for hours without collapsing into assistant voice. Long-term memory is also where DIY builds quietly fall apart: rolling summaries are a weekend of fiddling and still worse than what a tuned product does. Build it if you want privacy and your own characters, not if you came for the library.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define characters as persona cards and hold streaming, persistent, per-character conversations against a local or API model.
requirements: Ollama running locally, or an API key for any OpenAI-compatible provider in .env
A machine that can actually run a decent local model if you go the offline route
whatYouLose: The character library and its discovery feed: millions of cards you did not have to write
Models fine-tuned for persona persistence, so your build drifts back into helpful-assistant voice on long chats
Polished iOS and Android apps with push, background chats and voice calls
Shared chats, community rooms and the social loop around popular characters
Memory that holds up over hundreds of messages without you hand-rolling summarization
moatNotes: The tuning and the user-generated character corpus reinforce each other: the model stays in character, so people write more characters, so more people show up.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most users are not there to author a persona, they are there to browse thousands of them and start talking in ten seconds on a phone. The paid tier mostly buys queue priority and faster responses, which is the classic sign that the real product is capacity and catalog rather than features. A self-hosted clone wins on privacy, control and no content filter surprises, and loses on everything social. If your usage is two or three characters you wrote yourself, paying is hard to justify; if it is endless browsing, the DIY build is an empty room.
notes: The chat loop is trivial, the persona holding steady for two hours is not. Character cards are content, and content is somebody else's weekend, not yours.
prompt:
Build a local-first character roleplay chat app called Personae. Empty folder, no cloud services, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/personae.db, migrations in plain SQL run on boot
- Model access through one OpenAI-compatible client. Read OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY and MODEL_NAME from .env. Default the base URL to http://localhost:11434/v1 so Ollama works out of the box. Commit a .env.example, never a key.

Data model:
- characters: id, name, avatar_emoji, greeting, persona (long text), example_dialogue (long text), temperature, created_at
- chats: id, character_id, title, created_at
- messages: id, chat_id, role, content, token_estimate, created_at
- summaries: id, chat_id, up_to_message_id, content

Features in scope:
1. Character editor: create, edit, duplicate, delete. Import and export a character as a single JSON file so cards can be shared by hand.
2. Chat view: streaming assistant replies via Server Sent Events, markdown rendering, stop button, edit or delete any message, regenerate last reply, and a swipe-style alternative reply that keeps both and lets me pick.
3. Prompt assembly: system block from persona plus example dialogue, then the newest summary, then the last N messages that fit a configurable context budget. Show the assembled prompt behind a debug toggle.
4. Rolling memory: when a chat exceeds the budget, summarize the oldest unsummarized messages with the same model and store it in summaries. Summaries are visible and editable by me.
5. Full text search across all messages using SQLite FTS5.
6. Keyboard driven: new chat, character switcher, send, regenerate.

Out of scope, do not build: auth, multi user, voice, image generation, a character marketplace, mobile apps, analytics, payments.

Deliver a README with setup in under ten lines, a seed script that inserts two example characters, and Vitest coverage on prompt assembly and the summarization trigger. Run it and fix anything that breaks before you report done.
